fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-light or smoky conditions can identify it without delay.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris to allow full vehicle width for responding apparatus.
• Cut back dense vegetation that crowds the access drive to maintain a clear overhead and side clearance for larger emergency vehicles.
• Thin dense vegetation between the road and the main residence to reduce obstacles that could slow responders moving on foot.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure to keep the area around exterior walls open for responders working near the buildings.
• Keep the walkway and patio area clear of stored items, furniture, or equipment that could block responder movement around the structures.
• Establish a clearly visible staging area on the open lawn for responding units, and communicate its location to your local fire department in advance.
• Because rear access is limited to a single point, notify your local fire department of this constraint so they can plan accordingly before an incident occurs.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of the detached structure, access drive, and any rear access limitations.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim all tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the trees closest to the structure on all sides to create open space between the trunks and the building.
• Remove shrubs and ground vegetation growing directly against the exterior walls of the structure.
• Cut back or remove shrubs growing beneath the large trees near the structure to reduce the connection between ground-level plants and tree canopies.
• Thin the tree clusters visible near the structure so individual trees are separated by open space rather than touching or overlapping.
• Remove dead branches from the large trees near the structure and drop them to the ground for removal.
• Clear ground vegetation in the areas where scattered trees grow close to the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches from the scattered trees along the driveway.
• Trim back any shrubs or low branches along the driveway that narrow the travel lane or reduce visibility.
• Maintain the open clearing nearest the structure free of encroaching shrubs and ground vegetation.
• Move any stored wood, debris, or flammable materials away from the exterior walls of the structure.
• Regularly remove fallen leaves, needles, and dead plant material that accumulate against the structure and along the base of surrounding trees.
